advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add git-remote-s3 (with a hash pin) to a locked dependency group instead of an unhashed `uv pip install`, or install with `--require-hashes`.
evidence: `uv sync --locked --extra dev`
`uv pip install git-remote-s3==0.3.2`
Comment: "git-remote-s3 is the git transport helper ... it is NOT a rebar dependency ... so it is installed explicitly here"
ABSENCE: no `--require-hashes` / hash pin and the package is not recorded in the repo lockfile, so its transitive dependency graph is unpinned and unverified.
`curl -sSL "https://acli.atlassian.com/linux/${ACLI_VERSION}/acli_${ACLI_VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -o ~/.acli/acli.tar.gz`
`if [ -n "${ACLI_SHA256:-}" ]; then ... sha256sum -c --strict; else echo "::warning::ACLI_SHA256 unset — proceeding without checksum verification."`
ABSENCE: no fail-closed on missing digest — the download-and-exec path continues without verification.
`key: acli-${{ runner.os }}-${{ vars.ACLI_VERSION || 'unset' }}`
The download+verify step only runs `if: steps.cache-acli.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'`, so a cache hit skips verification entirely.
`- uses: actions/checkout@v7`
`- uses: actions/setup-python@v7`
`uses: actions/cache@v6`
`uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6`
Contrast: `uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c771a70e6277c0a99b617c7a806ffedaca235ff9  # v9.0.0` is SHA-pinned.
advisory.finding: `git-remote-s3==0.3.2` is installed via `uv pip install` outside the locked dependency set, so it (and its transitive deps) bypass the lockfile and are installed without hash/integrity verification.
merged_from: The `acli` binary is downloaded and executed with only conditional checksum verification: when `ACLI_SHA256` is unset the workflow proceeds without any integrity check (emits a warning and continues).

The acli cache key does not incorporate `ACLI_SHA256`, so if the pinned version's digest is corrected/rotated (or a poisoned tarball was cached under an unverified run) the stale/poisoned cache entry is reused on subsequent runs.
Newly-referenced GitHub Actions are pinned only to mutable major-version tags rather than immutable commit SHAs, unlike the co-located `astral-sh/setup-uv` which is SHA-pinned.
scenarios: A compromised or yanked release of git-remote-s3 0.3.2 or one of its transitive deps is pulled into the CI runner that holds a Jira API token and an S3-capable OIDC role.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `concurrency:` group to the jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal job (or scope the failure sweep to this run's own prefix) so the failure/cancel sweep cannot clobber a concurrent run's S3 objects.
evidence: aws s3 rm "s3://${REBAR_REHEARSAL_S3_BUCKET}/cloud-s3-rehearsal/" --recursive || true

Comment at :771 acknowledges the hazard for success ("sweeping the whole key-space on success would needlessly clobber a concurrently-running rehearsal") but the failure/cancel branch sweeps the whole key-space anyway
ABSENCE: no `concurrency:` block on the `jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal` job (:650-662) to serialize runs, while `on:` has both `workflow_dispatch` and a weekly `schedule` (:37-43)
advisory.finding: The failure/cancel S3 sweep deletes the entire shared `cloud-s3-rehearsal/` prefix recursively, but the job has no `concurrency:` guard; two overlapping runs (workflow_dispatch during the weekly schedule, or two dispatches within the 45m window) can have one run's failure sweep destroy a concurrently-running rehearsal's live store objects — the exact cross-run collision the comment claims to avoid on success.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `concurrency: { group: jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal, cancel-in-progress: false }` to the job, and/or narrow the sweep to the run-specific prefix rather than the shared `cloud-s3-rehearsal/` root.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make acli checksum verification mandatory (fail closed when ACLI_SHA256 is unset) rather than warning-and-proceeding, given the binary receives the live Jira token.
evidence: if [ -n "${ACLI_SHA256:-}" ]; then echo "${ACLI_SHA256}  $HOME/.acli/acli.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c --strict
else echo "::warning::ACLI_SHA256 unset — proceeding without checksum verification.
curl -sSL "https://acli.atlassian.com/linux/${ACLI_VERSION}/...tar.gz"
The same binary is then authenticated: `echo "$JIRA_API_TOKEN" | acli jira auth login` (:724)
advisory.finding: The acli binary download proceeds without integrity verification when ACLI_SHA256 is unset — it only emits a ::warning:: and continues — even though that binary is subsequently fed the live Jira API token, so a tampered/mirror-poisoned tarball would receive credentials.
advisory.suggested_fix: Treat an unset ACLI_SHA256 the same as an unset ACLI_VERSION: emit `::error::` and `exit 1` instead of `::warning::` and continuing.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Have `_plan_projects` fall back to the create payload's `_bridge_target_project` stamp (as the DC `_planned_projects` does) so CREATE-only plans are not scoped-vacuously.
evidence: `test_cloud_s3_rehearsal.py` `_plan_projects`: `target = entry.get("target")` then `if isinstance(target, str) and "-" in target: projects.add(target.split("-", 1)[0])` — no fallback to a create stamp

DC sibling `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py:99-106`: `_planned_projects` matches a Jira-key `target`, ELSE falls back to `(entry.get("fields") or {}).get(_BRIDGE_TARGET_PROJECT)`
acli.py:283 confirms CREATE payloads carry `_bridge_target_project` and have no key yet: `project = ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project") or self.jira_project`
dropped.finding: `_plan_projects` only derives a project from a plan entry's `target` key-prefix; it omits the create-payload `_bridge_target_project` stamp fallback that the DC sibling's `_planned_projects` uses. An inbound-CREATE plan entry has no Jira key yet (target is None/absent), so it contributes nothing to `planned`. `test_bridge_preview_read_only_and_scoped` then asserts `planned <= {REB, DIG}`, which passes vacuously when the plan is all CREATEs — the scoping check can never fail for the exact case (cross-project CREATE contamination) it is meant to catch.
scenarios: A preview plan composed of inbound CREATEs into a foreign project would not surface in `planned`, so the subset assertion passes despite contamination.
dropped.suggested_fix: Mirror the DC sibling: when `target` is not a Jira key, add `(entry.get("fields") or {}).get("_bridge_target_project")` to the project set.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_bridge_preview_read_only_and_scoped assert the plan is non-empty (or assert on an observable that is guaranteed populated) before checking `planned <= {REB, DIG}`, so the scoping claim cannot pass vacuously.
evidence: test asserts: `planned = _plan_projects(preview)` then `assert planned <= {REB_PROJECT, DIG_PROJECT}`
_plan_projects only adds a project when `isinstance(target, str) and "-" in target` (test_cloud_s3_rehearsal.py:_plan_projects)
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/manifest_renderer.py:51 `_target_of` returns `m.get('key','') or m.get('target','')` -> local_id/empty for inbound creates without a Jira key
A subset assertion against an empty set is trivially true, so a regression that mis-scoped an inbound-create plan would not be caught by this line.
dropped.finding: In test_bridge_preview_read_only_and_scoped, the plan-scoping assertion `assert planned <= {REB_PROJECT, DIG_PROJECT}` can pass vacuously: _plan_projects derives projects from each plan entry's 'target' prefix (target.split('-',1)[0]), but manifest_renderer._target_of returns a local_id or empty string for inbound-create mutations that carry no Jira key, and a fresh empty store's preview is inbound-create dominated. If `planned` is empty for any behavior, the subset assertion holds regardless of cross-project contamination, so the 'scoped, no cross-project contamination' claim (validation 3) is not actually exercised by this test; only the before/after count check has teeth.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly `git clone --branch tickets` (or clone then `git checkout tickets`) before reading projects.json, so a missing default HEAD fails with the mapping assertion, not FileNotFoundError.
evidence: `git_run(["git", "push", "rehearsal-s3", "tickets"], cwd=tracker)` pushes only the `tickets` branch

`git_run(["git", "clone", remote_url, str(clone)], cwd=tmp_path)` then `cloned_record = json.loads((clone / ".bridge_state" / "projects.json").read_text())` reads the working tree without an explicit `git checkout tickets`
The store's inner repo is created on branch `tickets` (conftest `rebar.init_repo`), not `main`, so the remote's default branch is not the conventional `main`
dropped.finding: `test_s3_store_roundtrips_with_mapping_intact` pushes only the `tickets` branch to S3, then does a bare `git clone <s3-url>` and immediately reads `clone/.bridge_state/projects.json`. This assumes the clone checks out a working tree from the pushed branch. If the git-remote-s3 remote does not advertise a default HEAD (a bare mirror push of a single non-`main` branch commonly leaves HEAD unset), `git clone` produces an empty/no-checkout working tree and the `.read_text()` raises a bare `FileNotFoundError` — an opaque failure rather than the intended mapping assertion, and not covered by an explicit checkout of `tickets`.
scenarios: A clone that does not check out `tickets` (no advertised HEAD / default-branch mismatch) yields no working-tree file, surfacing a confusing FileNotFoundError instead of the mapping-lost assertion.
dropped.suggested_fix: Clone with `git clone -b tickets remote_url clone` (or add a `git -C clone checkout tickets` step) before reading the record.
